input.content: Pattern: client/provider rollout coupling. In save_settings (client.py), the enhanced-settings increment began sending {"require_receipt": True} and hard-raising RuntimeError when response.get("applied") is not True — but the released provider returns only {"ok": True} and the provider-side receipt work (Task 2) ships in a separate repo and was still pending. Result: every ordinary save breaks against the supported provider, violating the design's "ordinary saves must continue to work at eval-release" / "independently releasable" constraints. Root cause: the new protocol was wired unconditionally instead of being gated behind the existing enhanced_settings feature flag (disabled by default). Lesson for review: when a client increment depends on a NEW provider capability, verify the provider side has shipped, and gate the new behavior behind the feature flag that already exists for it. Also: a test updated to return the new field (applied:True) masks the regression — require a backward-compat test exercising the old provider shape.
